title: 123. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Converting Compound Speed Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Converting Kilometres per Hour to Metres per Second
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in kilometres per hour to metres per second correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(54\text{ km/h}\) to \(\text{m/s}\).
questions.explanation: Convert both distance and time: \(54\times\frac{1{,}000}{3{,}600}=15\text{ m/s}\). The alternative \(194.4\text{ m/s}\) multiplies by \(3.6\), reversing the conversion.
questions.hint: Convert the numerator and denominator units separately.

questions.concept: Converting Metres per Second to Kilometres per Hour
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in metres per second to kilometres per hour correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(18\text{ m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\).
questions.explanation: The numerical speed is \(18\times 3.6=64.8\text{ km/h}\). The alternative \(5.0\text{ km/h}\) divides by \(3.6\) instead of multiplying.
questions.hint: Identify whether each unit conversion multiplies or divides the numerical rate.

questions.concept: Converting Kilometres per Hour to Metres per Second
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in kilometres per hour to metres per second correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(72\text{ km/h}\) to \(\text{m/s}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(\frac{72}{3.6}=20\text{ m/s}\). The alternative reverses the factor: \(72\times 3.6=259.2\).
questions.hint: Start from distance divided by time and keep the units visible.

questions.concept: Converting Metres per Second to Kilometres per Hour
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in metres per second to kilometres per hour correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(25\text{ m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(25\times 3.6=90\text{ km/h}\). The alternative reverses the factor: \(\frac{25}{3.6}\approx 6.94\).
questions.hint: Convert the numerator and denominator units separately.

questions.concept: Converting Kilometres per Hour to Metres per Second
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in kilometres per hour to metres per second correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(108\text{ km/h}\) to \(\text{m/s}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(\frac{108}{3.6}=30\text{ m/s}\). The alternative reverses the factor: \(108\times 3.6=388.8\).
questions.hint: Identify whether each unit conversion multiplies or divides the numerical rate.

questions.concept: Converting Metres per Second to Kilometres per Hour
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in metres per second to kilometres per hour correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(40\text{ m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(40\times 3.6=144\text{ km/h}\). The alternative reverses the factor: \(\frac{40}{3.6}\approx 11.11\).
questions.hint: Start from distance divided by time and keep the units visible.

questions.concept: Converting Kilometres per Minute to Metres per Second
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in kilometres per minute to metres per second correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(0.6\text{ km/min}\) to \(\text{m/s}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(0.6\times\frac{1{,}000}{60}=10\text{ m/s}\). The alternative converts kilometres to metres but omits converting minutes to seconds, giving \(600\).
questions.hint: Convert the numerator and denominator units separately.

questions.concept: Converting Metres per Second to Kilometres per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in metres per second to kilometres per minute correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(12\text{ m/s}\) to \(\text{km/min}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(12\times\frac{60}{1{,}000}=0.72\text{ km/min}\). The alternative converts seconds to minutes but labels \(720\text{ m/min}\) as kilometres per minute.
questions.hint: Identify whether each unit conversion multiplies or divides the numerical rate.

questions.concept: Converting Kilometres per Hour to Metres per Minute
questions.learningObjective: Convert a speed given in kilometres per hour to metres per minute correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(90\text{ km/h}\) to \(\text{m/min}\).
questions.explanation: Convert the distance and time units together: \(90\times\frac{1{,}000}{60}=1{,}500\text{ m/min}\). The alternative computes \(\frac{90}{60}=1.5\text{ km/min}\), then labels that number as metres per minute.
questions.hint: Start from distance divided by time and keep the units visible.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate an average speed in metres per second from distance and time given in kilometres and hours.
questions.question: A train travels \(180\text{ km}\) in \(2\text{ hours}\). What is its average speed in \(\text{m/s}\)?
questions.explanation: First find the speed in \(\text{km/h}\): \(\frac{180}{2}=90\text{ km/h}\). Then convert the distance and time units separately: \(90\text{ km}=90{,}000\text{ m}\) and \(1\text{ h}=3{,}600\text{ s}\), so the speed is \(\frac{90{,}000}{3{,}600}=25\text{ m/s}\). The alternative labels the \(\text{km/h}\) result as \(\text{m/s}\) without converting.
questions.hint: Convert the numerator and denominator units separately.
